audit_scope.description: This batch predominantly covers EL logic: EVM internals (memory, stack), transaction types (blob/EIP-4844, EIP-7702 authorizations), cryptographic primitives (ECDSA, KZG), P2P transaction propagation (eth/65), and JSON-RPC subscription APIs (EIP-758, EIP-8072). The Osaka and Prague fork specs are EL execution specs.

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, blob transactions with invalid KZG proofs, EIP-7702 authorizations with forged signatures, resource exhaustion via subscription flooding
Send invalid transaction announcements, bandwidth amplification via fake hash announcements, eclipse attacks, send invalid blob sidecars

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with invalid blob commitments, trigger chain reorganizations affecting transaction inclusion notifications

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component (opcode implementations calling memory buffer_read). Not an external entity—resides within the EVM execution boundary.
Governance/process entity (EIP author proposing upgrades). Not a runtime data source that sends data into the system at execution time. Irrelevant for runtime trust modeling.

Internal to EVM execution context. A smart contract calling a precompile is within the EL system boundary, not external. The actual external entity is whoever submitted the transaction triggering the contract.

From EIP-8072 context, this represents the local Ethereum node providing subscription service. From the EL system perspective, the node itself is the system under audit, not an external entity. The external entity is the user/DApp consuming the API.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_sendRawTransaction RPC (including blob type-3 transactions and EIP-7702 set-code transactions)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC endpoint. Any user can submit arbitrary transaction data including malformed blob transactions, invalid EIP-7702 authorizations, or transactions with crafted signatures. All data must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Subscription Client via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated RPC endpoint for subscriptions (EIP-758, EIP-8072). Clients can create unbounded subscriptions, potentially exhausting node resources. Filter parameters and transaction data must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via eth/65 P2P Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth/65 messages: NewPooledTransactionHashes (0x08), GetPooledTransactions (0x09), PooledTransactions (0x0a)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network peers. Can send fake transaction hash announcements for bandwidth amplification, return wrong transactions for requested hashes, or flood with oversized messages. All messages must be validated against size and count limits.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p block propagation including blob sidecars
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers can send blocks with invalid structure, malformed blob sidecars, or incorrect KZG proofs. Full block and blob validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: ECDSA Signature Provider (Transaction/Authorization Signer)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: ECDSA signature fields (r, s, v) in transactions and EIP-7702 Authorization structs
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Signature data originates from external signers and arrives via transactions. Invalid signatures, malformed r/s/v values, or crafted inputs targeting edge cases in secp256k1/P-256 recovery must be handled. The cryptographic validation (Legendre symbol check, curve point validation) is the trust boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Data Provider via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Blob sidecar gossip (blob data, KZG commitment, KZG proof)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blob data arrives via untrusted P2P gossip. Must verify KZG commitment matches versioned hash in transaction and KZG proof validates blob data authenticity. Relies on trusted setup integrity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Validator)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Proposed blocks for Osaka/Prague fork processing
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers are validators who may be malicious. Proposed blocks must pass full structural validation, transaction execution, state root verification, and blob gas limit checks. Fork activation logic must be deterministic regardless of proposer behavior.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All authorization fields (chain_id, address, nonce, y_parity, r, s) must be validated. Chain ID must match current chain or be zero. Signature must be cryptographically valid. Authority address must be correctly recovered.
All external byte data must pass type validation (correct length) before being used internally. Failure to validate could allow type confusion attacks.

Full blob transaction validation required: non-nil 'to' field, valid signature, at least one blob, versioned hash prefix 0x01, sufficient balance for execution + blob gas, max_fee_per_blob_gas >= current blob base fee.
Filter parameters (from, to addresses, hasReturnData) must be validated. Subscription resource limits must be enforced to prevent DoS. Connection lifecycle must be managed (cleanup on disconnect).

Mutual exclusion validation: exactly one of transaction or hash must be provided. If transaction provided, full eth_sendRawTransaction validation applies. Subscription timeout/resource limits must be enforced.

Message must not exceed 10MB devp2p limit. Max 4096 hashes (128KB). Duplicate announcements must be deduplicated. Bandwidth amplification must be mitigated by limiting concurrent GetPooledTransactions requests.
Returned transactions must be validated against requested hashes. Peers may return wrong transactions or empty responses. Full transaction validation required on received transactions.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block processing pipeline (Osaka/Prague validation, transaction execution, state trie update)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block structure validation, transaction execution under fork rules, state root verification, blob gas limit enforcement (MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK = 786432). Exception handling must properly rollback partial state changes.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Blob sidecar validation (KZG commitment verification, versioned hash matching)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Versioned hash must match kzg_to_versioned_hash(commitment). KZG proof must cryptographically verify blob data against commitment. Assumes KZG trusted setup integrity.

R coordinate must be validated on curve via Legendre symbol. Signature components must be within valid bounds. Point-at-infinity results must be rejected. P-256 public key must be validated as on-curve before verification. DER encoding must be correct.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Fork activation check and state transition (Osaka/Prague)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork activation must be deterministic based on block number/timestamp. Block processing must follow exact fork rules. All exceptions must trigger proper state rollback. Gas accounting must be correct.
